name: Constellation Energy Corporation

profile.description: Constellation Energy is the largest U.S. producer of carbon-free energy and, after closing its $16.4B Calpine acquisition in January 2026, the nation's largest electricity producer, operating the largest U.S. nuclear fleet plus Calpine's natural gas and geothermal assets. Q2 2026 reportable segment revenues were $7.24B (+40.7% YoY, including $2.15B from Calpine). Adjusted operating EPS was $2.55 and GAAP EPS $1.42, and full-year adjusted operating EPS guidance was raised to $11.50-12.50. In Q2 the company signed 920 MW of new long-term PPAs with investment-grade customers, including Walmart. The Crane Clean Energy Center (former Three Mile Island Unit 1) restart under a 20-year Microsoft PPA remains on track for 2H 2027, backed by a $1B DOE loan, NRC fuel license approval and FERC approval of capacity-rights transfer. TTM revenue is $31.27B.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Since its 2022 spin from Exelon, Constellation has made several transformative moves. These include the first U.S. restart of a retired nuclear unit (Crane, under a 20-year Microsoft PPA), the $16.4B Calpine acquisition that made it the largest U.S. power producer, and a shift toward long-dated contracts with investment-grade data-center and corporate buyers [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): Constellation powers AI data centers but does not ship AI products or report quantified internal AI savings [2]. Market Share (2/2): It is the largest U.S. electricity producer and the largest carbon-free producer, with Calpine contributing $2.15B of Q2 2026 segment revenue [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Crane restart is on track for 2H 2027, with the NRC fuel license amendment and FERC capacity-rights waiver secured. Another 920 MW of long-term PPAs were signed in Q2 2026, including a Walmart deal tied to a Dresden expansion [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): The company discloses no R&D spending, and growth capex does not count as R&D under the rubric [4].
innovation.label: STRONG

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Constellation's purpose of accelerating the transition to a carbon-free future through reliable nuclear power is specific. Strategic decisions such as restarting a retired reactor and signing 20-year carbon-free PPAs clearly trace back to it [2]. The company has only been independent since 2022, so it is not yet validated over decades. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive, dollar-quantified charitable programs were found in this screen's research. Economic impact from plant restarts is a byproduct of the business, not philanthropy [2]. Employee Retention (1/2): Constellation has been Great Place to Work Certified for four consecutive years, with 83% of surveyed employees calling it a great place to work [2]. That is positive sentiment, but no hard turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): Insider activity is net selling, including a Senior VP and Controller sale of ~$1.2M at $311 a share, and the Motley Fool notes that insider selling has weighed on the stock [3].
inspiration.label: DEVELOPING

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (yield 0.65%, below 2%; dividend paid since 2022). D/E 76.4% (score 0.972, 1x); ROE 15.1% (1.0, 2x); revenue growth 23.0% YoY (1.0, 1x); 5yr revenue CAGR 7.7% (FY2020 $17.6B predecessor to FY2025 $25.5B, derived from FMP; 0.847, 2x); Forward P/E 19.6 (1.0, 1x); profit margin 11.1% (0.554, 1x); Forward PEG 3.74 per Yahoo (0.0, 2x) [4]. Weighted sum 7.22 / 10 = 7.2, rounded to 7. The Yahoo PEG reflects a -46.8% YoY quarterly GAAP EPS decline as Calpine integration and mark-to-market effects depressed GAAP results, even though adjusted guidance was raised [1][4]. Liquidity is clear of the floor: 3.22M x $262.38 = ~$844M a day.
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): AI cannot replace nuclear and gas generation, and AI data-center load growth is a primary demand driver for Constellation's output [2]. The 20-year Microsoft PPA for the Crane restart exists specifically to power data centers, and the White House and PJM governors pushed for an emergency capacity auction amid rising load [2][3]. The residual risk is political: PJM and FERC have put a price collar on capacity prices to shield consumers [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): The 20-year Microsoft PPA tied to the Crane restart is a quantifiable, AI-driven revenue stream, and 920 MW of new long-term PPAs signed in Q2 2026 extend contracted demand from large-load customers [2].
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Constellation plays a mostly infinite game. Restarting a retired reactor at the Three Mile Island site under a 20-year contract, and making the $16.4B Calpine acquisition, are bets measured in decades, and four straight years of Great Place to Work certification suggest a culture that supports them. It falls short of fully infinite because its cause is only four years into independent life, and its competitive posture centers on scale and capturing data-center demand rather than learning from rivals.

just_cause.analysis: 2/3 pts. Reliable, carbon-free power at national scale is a genuine cause, and the Crane restart and 20-year PPAs show it shaping strategy [2]. Adding Calpine's gas fleet complicates the carbon-free narrative, and the cause has not yet been tested over decades as an independent company [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: 2/2 pts. Four consecutive years of Great Place to Work certification, with 83% of surveyed employees calling it a great place to work, point to a stable, trusted workforce in a safety-critical nuclear culture [2]. The June 2026 indictment of a former engineering manager for insider trading on Crane information is an individual matter, not a company finding [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: 0/1 pts. No management commentary was found that frames rivals such as Vistra or Talen as worthy rivals. Messaging centers on scale ('largest producer') and winning hyperscaler contracts [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: 1/2 pts. Constellation has evolved from a merchant generator spun out of Exelon into a contracted supplier of 24/7 power to tech and corporate buyers, and it added gas through Calpine [1][2]. This is a significant adaptation, but it has not abandoned a core business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: 2/2 pts. Committing more than a billion dollars and years of regulatory effort to restart Crane, at a site associated with America's worst nuclear accident, is a costly long-term bet [2]. So is the $16.4B Calpine acquisition, made despite a GAAP EPS decline in 2026 [1]. Leadership has held the 2H 2027 Crane target despite PJM signals of possible grid-connection delays to 2031 [2].

investment_thesis: Constellation is the scale leader in firm, carbon-free power just as AI data-center demand reshapes the U.S. grid. Q2 2026 segment revenue grew 40.7% to $7.24B with Calpine contributing $2.15B, adjusted EPS of $2.55 drove a $0.50 guidance raise to $11.50-12.50, and 920 MW of new long-term PPAs were signed [1][2]. The Crane restart under a 20-year Microsoft PPA has its NRC fuel license, FERC waiver and $1B DOE loan and is on track for 2H 2027 [2]. At 19.6x forward earnings with 15% ROE and 23% revenue growth, the valuation is reasonable for an AI-infrastructure enabler [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case starts with GAAP earnings, which are moving the other way: quarterly EPS fell 46.8% YoY, FY2025 GAAP EPS dropped to $7.40 from $11.89, and Yahoo's PEG of 3.74 shows weak trailing growth support [4]. Growth is increasingly coming from Calpine integration rather than organic nuclear performance, unplanned nuclear outages hit Q2, and the stock has fallen sharply from its peak [1]. Political risk is rising: PJM capacity price collars, calls for emergency auctions, and a PJM analysis suggesting Crane might not connect until 2031 could all cap economics [2][3]. Free cash flow was -$6.6B TTM per Yahoo Finance after the Calpine deal, and insiders are net sellers [3][4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings, where management said it would revisit the $11.50-12.50 adjusted EPS guidance [1]
Crane Clean Energy Center restart progress toward 2H 2027 grid connection under the 20-year Microsoft PPA [2]
Additional long-term data-center and corporate PPAs following 920 MW signed in Q2 2026, including the Walmart deal tied to the Dresden expansion [2]
key_risks: PJM capacity-market intervention (price collars, emergency auctions) reducing realized power prices [3]
Crane grid-connection delay: a PJM analysis suggested interconnection might not occur until 2031 [2][3]
Calpine integration and gas-fleet exposure diluting the carbon-free thesis, alongside GAAP EPS volatility (FY2025 $7.40 vs $11.89 in FY2024) [1][4]
